analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־
Proper noun, masculine singular, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר יַהְוֶה אֶל אַבְרָם, Yahweh speaks, and אֶל introduces Abram as the person he addresses.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition without a prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Clear the unsupported root אבה and its link to article 2bh. Preserve the explanation of the compound name and its recorded bearer.
draft.definition: Abram, the earlier name of Abraham, son of Terah.
draft.evidence: Genesis 11:26 identifies Abram as Terah’s son, and Genesis 17:5 records his change of name. The first element of אַבְרָם is the noun אָב, “father.” Neither verse supports deriving the name from אָבָה, “be willing.”

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר יַהְוֶה אֶל אַבְרָם, “Yahweh said to Abram,” אֶל introduces the addressee. The masculine singular command לֶךְ, “go,” is directed to him.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham

analysis.evidence: YHWH commands Abram to go from his land (מֵאַרְצְךָ) to the land he will show him (אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַרְאֶךָּ).
analysis.morphology: Qal imperative, second person masculine singular, addressed to Abram. The following לְךָ is a separate word.
